playbook:
When I must pledge, if I can only afford scout I pledge scout.

I always account that the pledge cost is deducted immediately from my fuel; plan endgame fuel value (unused fuel = points) when choosing costly pledges.

When I have ≥2 fuel and need immediate safe points (behind or close), prefer scout early rounds to bank points and conserve fuel.

When both opponents have been reliably scouting and I can commit, I will schedule a timed raid (pledge + act) in a round where I have the fuel and intention to perform it.

Never pledge raid as a bluff. I will only pledge raid if I intend to perform that raid on the act stage that same round and I have the fuel to pay the pledge cost now and still be able to accept any consequences.

When I am leading and an opponent to my left (who raids clockwise into me) is likely to raid, pledge escort to block theft.

When tied or slightly behind in late rounds and a clockwise raid would swing the score, pledge raid only if I will actually act raid that round and have the fuel to cover the pledge cost and any expected penalty.

When opponents show mixed signals (some scouts, some escorts) prefer escort if I’m vulnerable to incoming raids, or scout if I want guaranteed points and I’m not the raid target.

When submitting my act, always match my pledge. Do not plan to switch at act stage; treat the pledge as the committed action for that round.

When everyone pledged scout, prefer raid only if I pledged raid that round; otherwise choose scout or escort as pledged. Do not assume I can convert to a raid on the act stage without having pledged it.

When fuel is low (0–1), avoid pledging anything but scout; prioritize conserving fuel for end-of-game fuel-to-points conversion.

When deciding whether to raid, raid only if the clockwise target is scoring scouts without escort and the ±3 point swing materially helps my standing (taking into account opponents’ likely reactions next round).

If I expect a coordinated two-player raid on one target, use escort to protect that target if it’s me or scout elsewhere if I can’t protect.

If a previous raid attempt or pledge left me with too little fuel for future rounds (reducing endgame fuel value), avoid repeating that sequence—maintain enough fuel to secure leftover fuel points when that matters.

If leading near the end with low fuel, prioritize escort (if vulnerable) or scout to collect guaranteed points and preserve final fuel value rather than risky raids.

Require a simple fuel rule for raids: I will not pledge raid unless I have ≥2 fuel before the pledge and I am willing to have that fuel reduced immediately; I will ensure I can perform the pledged raid on the act stage.

Read opponent patterns: if two opponents repeatedly scout, one well-timed, executed raid can swing a tied late game—plan that only when I can and will execute it.

Keep commitments transparent: my pledges should reflect my intended acts so opponents can be predicted and I avoid miscoordination that wastes fuel.
